messages:
maria-customer: Hey team — we started getting 403s when the on-prem collector tries to upload debug bundles to our Private deployment. Request ID: 0a1b2c3d4e. Using presigned S3 URL from the console. Any quick repro steps we can run?

sam-support: Sorry you hit this — can you share the collector version and a minimal curl repro of the upload? usually it's either presign expiry, proxy, or redaction failing KMS.

jordan-eng: Also please paste a short log excerpt from the collector around the upload attempt (no need to send full bundle). look for lines with `upload`, `presign`, `403`, `signature`.

maria-customer: Collector version: 2.3.1-release. Log lines below (sanitized):
```
2026-03-17T14:03:12Z INFO collector: starting upload id=dbg-temp-01
2026-03-17T14:03:13Z WARN collector.upload: presign_response status=200 expires_in=30s id=dbg-temp-01
2026-03-17T14:03:15Z ERROR collector.upload: upload failed status=403 url=https://redwood-presign.s3.amazonaws.com/collections/abc123 req_id=0a1b2c3d4e
2026-03-17T14:03:15Z ERROR collector.redact: kms error: access denied for key arn:aws:kms:... redaction skipped
```

sam-support: thanks. couple of quick checks:
- presign expiry looks short (30s) — upload can fail if local machine clock drift or slow packaging. can you try a longer presign?
- KMS access denied for redaction will make collector try to upload unredacted bundle and fail if policy forbids. do you use a customer-managed KMS?

jordan-eng: For reproducing the HTTP failure locally, run this from the collector host (replace file):
```
curl -v -X PUT "https://redwood-presign.s3.amazonaws.com/collections/abc123" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \\
  --upload-file ./bundle.tar.gz
```
If that returns 403, capture `--trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt` and paste the TLS/proxy lines.

ops-oncall: also verify firewall/proxy: outbound 443 to S3 endpoints must be allowed; some customers route through a transparent proxy that strips auth headers.

maria-customer: ran curl, still 403. trace shows TLS handshake OK, but there is a corporate proxy rewriting `Expect` header. trace snippet: `Proxy: CONNECT redwood-presign.s3.amazonaws.com:443` then `HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established`. Not sure if that breaks presigned PUT.

sam-support: proxy rewrite can indeed break presigned PUTs. two options: 1) use chunked upload with POST+form (we can generate presigned POST), or 2) have presign generated with longer expiry and have collector stream via proxy-preserve headers. We can try presigned POST now.

collector-bot: presign-post created id=dbg-temp-01-post url=https://redwood-presign.s3.amazonaws.com/ POST-fields: {"policy":"<redacted>","x-amz-algorithm":"AWS4-HMAC-SHA256"} expires_in=300s

jordan-eng: @maria-customer can you run collector with `--upload-method post` or manually do: 
```
curl -v -F "key=collections/abc123/${filename}" -F "policy=<policy>" -F "x-amz-signature=<sig>" -F "file=@./bundle.tar.gz" https://redwood-presign.s3.amazonaws.com/
```
That usually survives proxies since it's a POST form upload.

maria-customer: Tried POST approach and upload succeeded. 👍 Bundle id: dbg-20260317-01. Collector logged `upload OK` and upload shows in console.

sam-support: great news! follow-ups:
- we'll add a note to docs about presign POST fallback for customers behind proxied networks.
- recommend increasing default presign expiry to 5m for Private collector builds.
- for the KMS redaction error, please open a support ticket with the KMS key ARN so we can validate IAM bindings; collector will attempt redaction again on next run.

maria-customer: opened ticket #CS-6123 with KMS ARN. thanks for the fast help.

jordan-eng: adding a small internal playbook: try POST presign if PUT returns 403 + proxy headers present; collect `collector.log` + `curl --trace-ascii` + `presign response` (remove policy body) and attach.

ops-oncall: noted — I'll patch collector to prefer POST when proxy detected in next minor release.

maria-customer: thanks team — upload + debug bundle verified, closing the incident on our side. :tada:
